title: Tuning mode
summary: Change a value in the running robot from AdvantageScope, and why only Tuning values can be written.

say.never: Most of AdvantageScope only **reads**: it shows you numbers the robot sends, like a speedometer. **Tuning mode** is different. It lets you **change** a number inside the running robot, like turning a dial while it drives. You see the result right away, with no need to stop and restart your code.
say.bit: AdvantageScope normally only reads values. **Tuning mode** also lets you write: change a number in the running robot and see the effect at once.

marks.label: only values under Tuning can be written
the starting value; a restart goes back to it

say.never: Tuning mode is how teams find the right numbers for a mechanism, like how hard to push a shooter wheel. You try a number, watch the graph, and try another. Two things to remember. Only numbers the robot code chose to publish in the **Tuning** table can be changed. And the robot forgets your change when it restarts, so when you find a good number, **write it into your code**.
say.bit: Teams use it to find numbers like a shooter speed or a PID gain without redeploying. Only values published under `Tuning` are writable, and a restart resets them, so copy the final value into your code.

say.never: The robot has to be running for tuning to work, because you're talking to the real program. Press **Start** and wait until the status says **Running**.
say.bit: Tuning talks to the running robot, so start it and wait for Running.

waitFor.hint: press Start and wait for Running.

say.never: Look at the top of the field list on the left, next to the search box. There is a small **slider icon**. That's the tuning button. If you can't see it, scroll the field list back to the top. If it's still missing, the robot hasn't published any tunable values yet, so make sure it's running and wait a few seconds.
say.bit: Next to the search box in the field list there's a slider icon: the tuning button. It only appears once the robot publishes values under Tuning. Scroll the list to the top if you can't see it.

waitFor.hint: find the slider icon next to the search box.

say.never: Click the slider icon (scroll the field list to the top if you can't see it). It turns **purple** when tuning mode is on. Click it again any time to turn it off. While it's on, the values you can change become editable boxes.
say.bit: Click the slider icon. It turns purple when tuning mode is on.

waitFor.hint: click the slider icon so it turns purple.

say.never: We want to change the flywheel's target speed. Type `FlywheelTargetRPM` in the search box. Look for the one under the **Tuning** table, not the one under AdvantageKit. Only the Tuning one can be changed.
say.bit: Search for `FlywheelTargetRPM` and pick the one under the Tuning table (not AdvantageKit).

say.never: Click the search result that starts with `Tuning/`. The field list scrolls to it.

Click in the box next to **FlywheelTargetRPM**, type a new number (the starting one is 3000, so try 3500), and press **Enter**. The robot now uses your number. Dozer can't read what you typed, so press **I did it** when you've done that, then **Verify** checks it for real.
say.bit: Type a different number than 3000 into the FlywheelTargetRPM box and press Enter. Press I did it when you have.

waitFor.hint: type a new value (not 3000), press Enter, then press I did it.

say.never: Open the lesson chip at the top and press **Verify**. The checker looks at the robot and sees that `FlywheelTargetRPM` is no longer 3000. That proves your change reached the robot. Remember: it forgets the new number when the robot restarts.
say.bit: Press Verify. The check reads FlywheelTargetRPM from the robot and wants it changed from 3000.
